samples.summary: `applyBorderPatch` re-implements `setStyle`'s read/merge/compact/delete body rather than reusing it (or a shared helper in `style-mutation.ts`)
samples.evidence: Lines 4132-4157 duplicate `setStyle` (3712-3728) almost verbatim — `store.get(anchor) || {}`, `mergeStylePatch`, `compactCell`, `isEmptyCell` -> `store.delete`, else `store.set` — with only the pruning loop and the equality short-circuit added. A `setStyle(ref, patch, { pruneDefaultsInRange })` option, or extracting the write tail into `style-mutation.ts` alongside `compactCell`/`isEmptyCell`, would keep the two write paths from drifting. Also note `applyBorderPatch` skips `normalizeRefToAnchor` that `setStyle` applies, relying on `collectBorderTargets` having already anchored — an implicit precondition the extracted primitive would have made explicit. Taste/structure only; the behaviour matches the task doc's stated approach (docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheets-clear-borders-prune-todo.md:26-38).

samples.summary: Design doc says `compactCell` "now carries" spill fields, but this change makes no functional change there — only a comment rewrite
samples.evidence: The diff for packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/style-mutation.ts touches only the doc comment above `compactCell`; the spill-field copies (lines 70-81) are unchanged, so spill carry-over predates this PR. Wording the design doc as a change introduced here ('which now carries…') mis-records the history, and the whole bullet plus the new spill round-trip test is scope beyond issue #878 ('Clear borders should remove the border keys'). Suggest stating it as existing invariant the border path relies on.
